label: TMUA 2020 · Paper 2 · Question 18

hints.title: Study the difference as one polynomial
hints.body: Set h=f−g. Its coefficients are a−p, b−q, c−r and d−s, and h(x)>0 must hold for every real x.
hints.recap: Global positivity is a condition on the difference.
hints.pitfall: The difference of two cubics can have lower degree.
hints.pause: Write h explicitly and inspect its leading coefficient.

recall.reminder: A nonzero cubic has opposite-sign tails and cannot stay positive on the entire real line.

hints.title: Test both ends of the real line
hints.body: Consider what happens to the sign of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></math> for large positive and large negative <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></math> if its cubic coefficient is nonzero.
hints.recap: An odd leading power has opposite signs at the two ends.
hints.pitfall: Positivity at one end alone does not satisfy an every-input condition.
hints.pause: Determine what the hypothesis forces about the cubic coefficient.

recall.reminder: An odd leading power has opposite signs at the two ends.

hints.title: Inspect the reduced polynomial
hints.body: Now impose <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>q</mi></mrow></math> in your reduced difference and examine whether its remaining degree is compatible with positivity for every real input. Separately evaluate the difference at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: Degree reduction and a convenient input reveal different coefficient restrictions.
hints.pitfall: The difference may reduce to a constant; do not insist on a quadratic term.
hints.pause: Derive the remaining restrictions and use them to assess II and III.

recall.reminder: Degree reduction and a convenient input reveal different coefficient restrictions.

solution:
Write h(x)=f(x)−g(x)=(a−p)x3+(b−q)x2+(c−r)x+(d−s). By assumption h(x)>0 for every real x.

A nonzero cubic coefficient would force opposite signs as x tends toward the two ends of the real line. Hence a−p=0, so a=p. Statement I, a>p, is false.

If b=q, then h(x)=(c−r)x+(d−s). A nonzero slope would again make h negative in one direction. Thus c=r whenever b=q, proving II.

At x=0, positivity gives d−s>0, so d>s, proving III. These arguments also permit h to be a positive constant; they do not assume a surviving quadratic term.

Answer G: II and III only.
knowledgePattern: Use global polynomial positivity to force leading cancellations
